title: Speaking Part 4 — the abstract one
note:
Part 4 is Part 1's shape at Part 3's stakes: react, state a view, expand, and then bring in the other candidate. What makes it its own thing is the GENERALISE move — 'Generally speaking, people are very busy' rather than 'I'm very busy'. Part 1 asks about you; Part 4 asks about people, and answering it personally is the commonest way to lose the band.

So in every generalise round one distractor is the same content said about yourself. Nothing else needed inventing: the wrong answer is the right answer in the wrong person.

The last round has no equivalent anywhere else in the exam. The examiner turns to the second candidate, who has to refer to the first BY NAME and then add something of their own — Interactive Communication and Discourse Management in one turn.

x.name: React
x.hint: take a position before you defend it

g.name: Generalise
g.hint: about people, not about you — this is the Part 4 move

c.name: Concede
c.hint: the side that cuts against you

p.name: Involve Lucas
p.hint: agree or disagree by name, then add your own
